chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from al-Nadr from Hisham from Sulayman ibn Khalid said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who leads the people in prayer and then advances a man who has already missed one rak'ah, asking what he should do. He said: 'He should not advance the man who has missed one rak'ah, but rather he should take the hand of another and advance him.'

This report, although its apparent meaning is prohibition, is diverted from it to the side of preference (karam), as we have previously mentioned based on the preceding reports. And if the Imam dies before completing his prayer, he should be laid aside, and the people should advance whoever will pray the remainder of what is upon them, and whoever touches him should perform ghusl. This was narrated.

key_terms.بَقِيَّةَ مَا عَلَيْهِمْ: The remainder of what is upon them
key_terms.فَلْيُطْرَحْ: He should be laid aside/set aside
key_terms.وَيَغْتَسِلُ: And he should perform ghusl (ritual bath)
key_terms.يُحْدِثُ: To advance or move forward (a person in prayer)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if the Imam dies during congregational prayer and how should the follower who missed a rak'ah be handled?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* elucidates the hierarchy of preference in congregational leadership, noting that while advancing a latecomer is permissible, it is superior to appointing another qualified individual. It further details the practical jurisprudence of *imamat al-mawt* (leadership during death), specifying that the deceased Imam is set aside and the congregation continues, with ritual bath (*ghusl*) required for those who touch him, reflecting the Shia emphasis on ritual purity and continuity of worship.
